faces.name: Rad
faces.subtitle: Big Time & Data
faces.short: The time on one line in large figures in the style of road signs, with the date and two readings in large type under it: all of it readable without glasses.
full: Rad sets the time on a single line, as wide as the round screen allows at its height, in condensed figures in the style of road signs: lettering made to be read at a distance and at speed. The hours are white, the colon and the minutes the colour of your theme.

Around it, the things you check every day are large too. The date sits above the time in your watch's own language, battery and alerts above it. Under the time, two readings stand in rounded chips, each with its icon: heart rate and steps to start, or the weather, Body Battery, calories, distance, sunrise and sunset or any of fifteen sources. The chips size themselves to what they hold. Below them a short bar fills as your steps meet their goal, or floors, intensity minutes, Body Battery, battery or stress.

Six themes in the colours of road signs: Yellow, Green, Blue, Orange, White and Paper, dark figures on a white ground for anyone who reads better that way. 12 and 24 hour time, without a leading zero in 12 hour. The always-on mode keeps the time at the same size in a light weight.

faces.name: Stor
faces.subtitle: Extra Large Numbers
faces.short: The time in figures as tall as your watch allows, hours over minutes, so you can read it at arm's length without your glasses.
full: Stor puts the time in the largest figures a round screen can hold: the hours on one line, the minutes on the next, each nearly a third of the screen's height. Heavy, open figures in a modern grotesque, white on black, with the minutes in a colour of your choice, read at a glance across a room, in the car or first thing in the morning before your glasses are on.

Everything else stays out of the way. A thin bar between the two lines fills as your steps meet their goal, so progress needs no reading at all; it can follow floors, intensity minutes, Body Battery, battery or stress instead, or be switched off. Battery and alerts sit at the top. The date sits at the foot in your watch's own language, or put one reading there instead: heart rate, the weather, steps or any of fifteen sources.

Six themes: Coral, Amber, Mint, Sky, Mono and Paper, dark figures on a white ground for anyone who reads better that way, and for a bright day on a memory-in-pixel screen. 12 and 24 hour time, without a leading zero in 12 hour. The always-on mode keeps the same figures at the same size in a hairline weight, large enough to read in the dark.

faces.name: Däck
faces.subtitle: Tyre Analog
faces.short: An analog face drawn as a racing wheel: the tyre's coloured band fills with your steps, the date is moulded into the sidewall.
full: Däck is an analog face drawn as a racing wheel seen from the side. The tyre runs out to the edge of the glass, its coloured band filling from twelve o'clock as your steps fill their goal; it can follow floors, intensity minutes, Body Battery, battery or stress instead. The date, in your watch's own language, is moulded into the sidewall at six.

Inside the rim, the wheel cover is the dial: hour marks, two hands outlined so they read over everything, and a hexagonal centre-lock nut ringed in the compound's colour. Three readings sit at nine, three and six o'clock, each any of fifteen sources: heart rate, the weather and Body Battery to start, or steps, calories, distance, floors, intensity minutes, stress, pressure, elevation, the next sunrise or sunset, notifications or battery. Battery and alerts sit at twelve.

The five themes are the five tyre compounds: Soft (red), Medium (yellow), Hard (white), Intermediate (green) and Wet (blue). The always-on mode keeps the lit band as a hairline, the hour marks and the hands' outlines.

faces.name: Bana
faces.subtitle: Circuit Map
faces.short: A circuit map round your dial: a car laps it once an hour, its trail marks the minutes, and the time sits in the infield.
full: Bana draws a race circuit round your dial, with a long straight across the top, esses down the right, a chicane along the bottom and kerbs at the corners. A car laps it once an hour: it stands on the chequered line at the top of every hour, a quarter of the way round at a quarter past, and the lap so far is lit behind it. The circuit is invented, not any real track.

The time sits in the infield in Tomorrow, with three readings under it, each any of fifteen sources: heart rate, steps and the weather to start, or calories, distance, floors, intensity minutes, Body Battery, stress, pressure, elevation, the next sunrise or sunset, notifications or battery. When a reading runs long, the row steps down a size together. Battery and alerts sit above the circuit, and the date, in your watch's own language, below it.
Five themes: Night, Grass, Day (light), Neon and Mono. The always-on mode keeps the circuit as a hairline, the car and the time in a light cut.

faces.name: Varv
faces.subtitle: Timing Screen
faces.short: A race timing screen: the time on a slanted panel, your goals as three sectors that turn purple when met, and the day as a lap.
full: Varv reads like the timing screen on a race broadcast. The time sits on a slanted panel in Exo 2 Italic, a stripe in the theme's colour at its end. Above it, the lap: today's day of the year over the days in it, LAP 276/365 on the third of October.

Under the time, three sectors, one for each of your goals: steps, floors and intensity minutes by default. A sector turns purple when its goal is met, green while you are ahead of the pace that meets it by ten at night, and yellow when you are behind; intensity minutes are paced across the week. Each sector's icon, in the same colour, sits over its value. Two more readings below are any of fifteen sources: heart rate and the weather to start, or calories, distance, floors, Body Battery, stress, pressure, elevation, the next sunrise or sunset, notifications or battery. The date, in your watch's own language, sits on a slanted tag at the bottom.
Five themes: Studio, Carbon, Day (light), Teal and Neon. The always-on mode keeps the time in a light cut and the sectors as outlines in their colours.

faces.name: Kod
faces.subtitle: The Minute as a Diff
faces.short: The time as a code change: the minute just gone removed on a red line, now added on a green one, with your data as bullet lines below.
full: Kod shows the time the way a developer reads changes: as a diff. Under a hunk header carrying the date, the minute that has just gone is removed on a red line and the current one is added on a green one, larger, in Geist Mono. It follows your 12 or 24 hour setting, so at the top of the hour 11:00 removes 10:59.

Below, three bullet lines, each any of fifteen sources: heart rate, steps and the weather to start, or calories, distance, floors, intensity minutes, Body Battery, stress, pressure, elevation, the next sunrise or sunset, notifications or battery. A source with a goal adds a five-cell stat of plus and minus signs, and its bullet turns green when the goal is met.
Under a prompt with a steady cursor, your Body Battery reads as the context you have left: or battery, steps, floors, intensity minutes or stress, or nothing. Battery and alerts sit at the top.
Five themes: Graphite, Paper (a light editor), Midnight, Mono and Neon. On memory-in-pixel screens every theme is drawn for 64 colours. The always-on mode keeps the added minute and the prompt.

faces.name: Tanke
faces.subtitle: Thinking Terminal
faces.short: A terminal that thinks: the time in a rounded box, a spinner with a new verb every minute, and your goals as a to-do list that ticks itself off.
full: Tanke is a terminal session on your wrist, one where something is always thinking. The time sits in a rounded box with the date, in Red Hat Mono, on warm black with a terracotta accent.
Under it, an asterisk spinner turns a frame a minute beside a verb: Pondering, Brewing, Noodling, Percolating, twenty-four of them, a new one every minute and never the same twice running.

Your goals hang off it as a to-do list. Each line is a checkbox, an icon, your progress and the goal your watch keeps: steps, floors and weekly intensity minutes to start, or Body Battery, battery or stress. A goal you meet is ticked and struck through; the first one still open is the one in progress. At the bottom, a prompt box with a steady cursor, and battery and alerts at the top.

Five themes: Clay, Ivory (a light terminal), Sage, Iris and Mono. On memory-in-pixel screens every theme is drawn for 64 colours. The always-on mode keeps the time and the thinking line. The cursor does not blink, because a blink would wake the watch every second.

The horizon is your progress. It lights from the left as your steps add up, glow and all, with a flare at the leading edge like the sun coming up over a planet seen from orbit. Meet your goal and it is lit end to end. It can follow floors, intensity minutes, Body Battery or battery instead.

Above it, the time in Unbounded, a wide and heavy face, with the date in your watch's own language and battery and alerts. On the planet's dark side, three readings you choose from fifteen: heart rate, Body Battery and the weather to start, or steps, calories, distance, floors, intensity minutes, stress, pressure, elevation, the next sunrise or sunset, notifications or battery.

Five themes: Void, black and white, and Solar, Ice, Nebula and Mars, which tint the light. On memory-in-pixel screens every theme is drawn for 64 colours. The always-on mode keeps the time and the lit horizon as a hairline.

faces.short: Your watch as a terminal: seven lines of data, each with a bar towards its goal or a two-hour sparkline, under the time in a monospace face.

Every line can show any of fifteen sources: heart rate, steps, Body Battery, stress, pressure, elevation, the weather, calories, distance, floors, intensity minutes, the next sunrise or sunset, notifications or battery, or nothing at all. Lower lines hold fewer cells, so nothing runs off the round screen.

Above them, the time in JetBrains Mono, the day in your watch's own language with the date written the ISO 8601 way, and battery and alerts. Below them, a prompt and a steady block cursor; it does not blink, because a blink would wake the watch every second.
Five themes: Phosphor, Amber, Ice, Paper and Plasma. On memory-in-pixel screens every theme is drawn for 64 colours. The always-on mode keeps the time and the prompt.

faces.pitch: Read your day like a dashboard.

Three gauges sit at nine, three and six o'clock, each with its own scale, a filled arc, a needle, an icon and the value: Body Battery, steps and intensity minutes by default, or battery, floors and stress. The hour and minute hands are outlined in the dial's colour so they read cleanly over a gauge, and a minute track runs round the rim. Every figure is set in Saira.

Five themes: Carbon, Steel, Navy, Racing and Arctic, a white dial. On memory-in-pixel screens every theme is drawn for 64 colours. The always-on mode keeps the hands in outline, the hour markers and the date.

faces.name: Vecka
faces.subtitle: Weekly Activity Chart
faces.short: Your week as seven bars: every day against its goal, last week's days still to come, the week's total and average, and weekly intensity minutes round the rim.
full: Vecka shows your week the way your watch has been keeping it: seven bars, one a day, from the first day of the week your watch is set to. A day that met its goal is lit in the accent, a day that fell short is dim, and today is bright and still growing. A dashed line marks the goal.

The days still to come show last week's same days in outline, so there is always something to beat. Under the bars, each day's initial in your watch's language; under those, the week's total, the daily average and how many days met their goal so far.

Above the chart, today's figure against its goal, the time in Space Grotesk and the date with the ISO week number. Round the rim, your weekly intensity minutes against Garmin's weekly goal, with the figure where the ring begins. Battery and alerts sit at the top.

The bars can show steps, calories, distance, floors or the day's intensity minutes. Five themes: Ink, Coral, Forest, Mono and Paper. On memory-in-pixel screens every theme is drawn for 64 colours. The always-on mode keeps the time and the week's bars in outline.

faces.name: Kurva
faces.subtitle: Sensor History Charts
faces.short: Four sensors' last hours as charts, one above the other: heart rate, Body Battery, stress and pressure, each with its high and low.
full: Kurva puts the history your watch has been recording all along on the dial. Four rows, one sensor each: its icon, its value now, its last hours drawn as an area under a line, and the high and the low of that span.

Every chart sits in the same columns, so all four share one clock. A morning run is a peak in heart rate, a step down in Body Battery and a gap in stress, one above the other. Where the watch took no reading the chart leaves a gap; it never draws a guess as a zero.

Each row can show heart rate, Body Battery, stress, barometric pressure or elevation, and the charts reach back 2, 4, 8 or 12 hours. Two more readings sit at the bottom, from fifteen sources: steps, calories, distance, floors, intensity minutes, the weather, the next sunrise or sunset and more. The time is set large in Inter Tight, with the date in your watch's own language, and battery and alerts at the top.

Each sensor keeps its own colour in every row. Five themes: Night, Slate, Paper, Mono and Amber. On memory-in-pixel screens every theme is drawn for 64 colours. The always-on mode keeps the time and the four lines.

faces.subtitle: Doodle Notebook
faces.short: A doodled notebook page whose star, lightning bolt and flame get coloured in as your goals fill, and turn into stickers.
full: Klotter is a page from a school notebook on your watch: squared paper, a red margin line, a smiley and a spiral scribbled in the corners, and the time written large in a marker hand over a yellow highlighter stripe.

Under the time are three doodles, outlined in pen, and they are your goals. The star is your steps, the lightning bolt your Body Battery and the flame your intensity minutes. Each one is coloured in with marker from the bottom up as its goal fills, and when a goal is met the doodle turns into a sticker: coloured in solid, edged in white, with a little sparkle. Each doodle's reading is written under it.
The date sits above the time in your watch's own language, underlined by hand, with battery and alerts at the top.

Five papers: a white notebook in blue pen, brown kraft in black marker, a chalkboard, a blueprint and a midnight page with neon markers. Every doodle can follow steps, Body Battery, intensity minutes, floors, battery or stress.
On memory-in-pixel screens the notebook is white paper, which reads best in sunlight, and every page is drawn for 64 colours. The always-on mode keeps the three doodles' outlines and the time.

faces.name: Hoppa
faces.subtitle: Pixel Platformer
faces.pitch: Your day is a game level.
faces.short: A pixel-art game level on your watch: a cat runs to the flag as you walk, collecting coins, with Body Battery as its hearts.
full: Hoppa turns your day into a level of a pixel-art game. The bottom of the dial is the level: grass over brick, a hill, a row of gold coins and a flag at the far end. The hero is a ginger cat in a red scarf, and it runs on your steps. Each morning it starts at the left; as you walk it runs right, collecting every coin it passes, and when your step goal is met it reaches the flag, the flag goes up and the cat jumps.

Above the level, five hearts are your Body Battery, like a game's health bar, filling half a heart at a time. The time is drawn in big pixel figures, built block by block for each screen so they stay perfectly sharp, with a drop shadow as a game's score has. Two readings sit under it, heart rate and steps to start with, and the date and battery at the top.

Five worlds: a blue-sky meadow, a starry night, a sunset desert, snow and lava. The cat can run on steps, Body Battery, intensity minutes, floors or battery, and the hearts can show any of them but stress.

On memory-in-pixel screens every world is drawn in flat 64-colour pixel art, as a console would draw it. The always-on mode keeps the figures as dots, the ground line, the cat's outline and the flag pole.

faces.name: Raket
faces.subtitle: Rocket to the Moon
faces.pitch: Walk your rocket to the moon.
faces.short: A rocket flies round the dial from the Earth to the moon as you walk, and lands when your step goal is met.
full: Raket is a space mission on your watch. The Earth sits at the lower left of the dial and the moon at the upper right, and a little rocket flies between them round the edge: that flight is your step goal. Each morning the rocket waits on the launch pad; as you walk it climbs over the top of the dial, a trail of puffs behind it and a dotted path ahead, and when the goal is met it lands beside the moon in a sparkle.
The moon is drawn in its real phase, tonight's, worked out on the watch. Stars and a ringed planet fill the rest of the sky.

The time is set large in Bungee, a bold signage typeface, with the date above it in your watch's own language. Two readings sit under the time, heart rate and steps to start with, then battery and alerts.
Five missions: classic navy with a red rocket, retro teal, galaxy violet, Mars rust and night black. The rocket can fly on steps, Body Battery, intensity minutes, floors or battery instead.

On memory-in-pixel screens every mission is drawn for 64 colours; on AMOLED everything is anti-aliased. The always-on mode keeps the path ahead as dots, the rocket's outline, the Earth and the moon, and the time.

faces.name: Kompis
faces.subtitle: Pocket Pet
faces.pitch: A pet that lives on your watch.
faces.short: A little pet that lives on your watch: its hearts fill with your steps, and its mood follows your Body Battery.
full: Kompis is a small round creature with pointed ears and a sprout on its head, and it lives on your watch. Five hearts sit under it, and they are your step goal: each heart is a fifth of the goal, filling half a heart at a time. When all five are full, Kompis throws its arms up and confetti falls.

Its mood is your Body Battery. Rested, it bounces with its eyes shut tight and its mouth wide open; as the day goes on it is happy, then tired, with heavy eyelids, and worn out, with a drop of sweat, when your battery runs low. At bedtime it goes to sleep, from the sleep time in your Garmin profile to your wake time, and wakes up with you. Sleep can be turned off.

The time is set large in Baloo 2, a round and friendly typeface, with the date above it in your watch's own language. Two readings sit beside the pet, heart rate and steps to start with, and battery and alerts at the foot.
Five colours of Kompis: mint, peach, berry, sky and lemon. The hearts can fill with steps, Body Battery, intensity minutes, floors or battery instead, and the mood can follow any of them but stress.
On memory-in-pixel screens Kompis is drawn for 64 colours; on AMOLED it is anti-aliased. The always-on mode shows Kompis asleep, as a fine outline, and the time.

faces.name: Pärla
faces.subtitle: Pearl & Rose Gold
faces.short: A jewellery analog: mother-of-pearl, rose-gold hands, cut stones at the hours and a pearl that rides to your step goal.
full: Pärla is a dress watch for every day. The dial is mother-of-pearl, its nacre laid in soft rings of pearl, blush and pale blue; round it runs a rose-gold chapter ring and minute track, with a cut stone at each hour and a crown of three at twelve. The hands are dauphine, faceted along their ridge so one side catches the light and the other falls into shadow, and they turn on a pearl set in rose gold.

At six a sub-dial carries a pearl along its arc toward your step goal, with the count at its centre; at three a small window holds heart rate, or any reading you choose. Under the crown, the date in your watch's own language, and battery and alerts.
Five dials: pearl, blush, champagne with yellow gold, a black Tahitian pearl, and sapphire with white gold. The sub-dial can follow steps, Body Battery, stress, intensity minutes, floors or battery.

The lettering is Cormorant Garamond. On memory-in-pixel screens the light dials are drawn as clean white, pink and cream plates that read best in sunlight; on AMOLED the nacre and the hands are anti-aliased. The always-on mode keeps the hands and a stone at each quarter.

faces.pitch: A vintage instrument for your wrist.

Below the tubes, a working VU meter: a backlit scale from 0 to 100 with a red zone, and a needle that tracks your step goal, or Body Battery, stress, floors, intensity minutes or battery. Either side, four neon lamps light when your phone is connected, messages are waiting, an alarm is set or do-not-disturb is on. The date is engraved on a brass plaque above the tubes, and a second plaque below carries the reading of your choice: battery, heart rate, weather, sunset and more.

Five tube colours (neon orange, magic-eye green, argon blue, violet and white) and three case finishes (brass, blackened steel and copper), chosen independently. The always-on mode keeps the numerals as thin wire, at 1% of pixels lit.
